 Growth estimates are quantified as transition probabilities.

 Growth formulated in terms of transition probabilities readily

Connecting Growth to Policy

 Presently, the NCLB goal of universal proficiency by 2014 is
 written into accountability systems in terms of higher-and-higher
 levels of achievement.
 A valid criticism of such systems is that they fail to recognize
 highly effective schools that work with low performing students.

 Examining growth/effectiveness, does not make universal
 proficiency easier to achieve.
 For example, in order for 2014 universal proficiency to exist for

 must become partially proficient (i.e., NCLB proficient) in 4th
 grade.

 Presently, the NCLB goal of universal proficiency by 2014 is
 written into accountability systems in terms of higher-and-higher

 highly effective schools that work with low performing students.
